The tax takes a bigger share from higher earners, and Acts 46 and 24 are reshaping it. It raised $3.29 billion in FY2025 (pp. 3, 28, 35).
Hawaiʻi's biggest tax hits business sales at every step. It raised $4.63 billion in FY2025, 40.4 percent of state taxes (pp. 3, 56).
Taxing visitors can help residents, but only if residents are paid back for what they pay too. The hotel and rental tax raised $816.2 million in FY2025 (pp. 73–74, 77).
Homeowners pay the lowest property tax rate in the country, 0.29 percent of home value against 0.90 percent nationally, and only counties can set it (pp. 87–88).
The corporate tax raised $400.4 million net in FY2025. UHERO says a large rate cut could raise total revenue, based on 2010 data it will revisit (pp. 101, 107).
An annual wealth tax is unlikely to raise much if Hawaiʻi acts alone. Estate tax revenue is lumpy: $405.8 million in FY2025, including a one-time $315 million payment (pp. 118, 120).
Credits are spending by another name: $621.3 million claimed in 2023 (p. 133). 72 percent of the solar credit claimed on individual returns went to filers earning $100,000 or more (p. 147).
